title: Porridge with apple and rhubarb compote

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Oats, fresh fruit, sugar, cinnamon and walnuts are all plain cupboard and garden foods with nothing factory-made.

supermarket.reason: Every ingredient, including March rhubarb and walnuts, is an everyday Tesco item at a normal price.

basic_kitchen.reason: Two saucepans and a wooden spoon are all it needs, and the techniques are simmering and stirring.

works.reason: 200g oats to 1.2 litres water is the standard porridge ratio for four, and the compote amounts, liquid and 10-minute covered simmer are sound.

honest_times.reason: Twelve minutes covers coring and chopping three apples and the rhubarb, zesting and juicing an orange and chopping walnuts, and the 10-minute cook matches the steps for a quick breakfast.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning is used, names match their ids and nothing unlisted appears apart from water.

seasonal_feel.reason: Warm porridge suits a chilly March morning, and stored apples lead the compote, with early rhubarb in support.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are clear, homely British English with no restaurant language or preaching.

hearty_healthy.reason: Oat porridge with fruit compote and walnuts is a filling, real-food breakfast with only modest added sugar.
